## Context / Problem

Epic 62dc's criterion 5 is undelivered: plan review does not tell a reviewer that the plan under review overlaps work already described by another ticket. A reviewer reads one plan in isolation, so two tickets that plan the same change both pass, and the duplication is found later in code review or not at all.

Create-time surfacing catches a duplicate at the moment of filing, when the only evidence is a title and a short description. Plan review runs later against a full plan, which is far more material to match on, and is the last gate before work starts. The same index serves both.

## Approach

**Reuse the index; add no second retrieval path.** The sibling index story builds a lexical FTS5 index under `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/` that persists a map from ticket directory to its last-indexed dir hash, and refreshes it by enumerating the live ticket-directory set and diffing it against that map. Catch-up is synchronous in the read phase, with no daemon. That index is already reachable through one public function, `find_similar` (`src/rebar/similar/__init__.py:46-54`), and the package states at `:8` that this one function is its whole surface. It **already** accepts arbitrary query text via `text=` (`:51`, resolved at `:73`) and already keeps a ticket out of its own results via `exclude_id=` (`:52`), so querying it with plan material needs no new retrieval module and no second path. If the optional embedding tier is configured the query ranks through it, otherwise it ranks lexically (`:79-82`), so overlap detection inherits the sibling's portability: it works with no model provider configured, and is unavailable in no installation.

**The one gap is failure distinguishability, and that is what this ticket adds to the retrieval surface.** `find_similar` deliberately collapses every failure mode to an empty list -- an absent index returns `[]` (`:63-64`), a catch-up failure warns and returns `[]` (`:67-72`), and any other exception warns and returns `[]` (`:83-85`), the "Never raises" property at `:55`. A caller cannot tell an absent index from a failed catch-up from a corpus that simply matched nothing. Two of this ticket's acceptance criteria require exactly that distinction, because they demand a recorded diagnostic rather than a silent skip. The change is an opt-in diagnostic signal on the existing function, not a parallel retrieval entry point.

**Ride the existing Pass-1 extra-context seam.** A Pass-1 finder unit already accepts store-derived `extra_context` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/checkpoints.py:54`), and its identity binds that context by `context_digest`, a sha256 over the injected text (`:61-63`, carried at `:70`), under the Pass-1 discovery contract `plan_review_findings` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:122`). The text itself is built by `_chunk_extra_context` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:215`), whose single call site at `pass1.py:326` feeds both `_discovery_unit_plan(extra_context=...)` at `:331` and `checkpoint_identity(extra_context=...)` at `:339`; `checkpoints.py` only *accepts* the parameter and never builds it, so `pass1.py` is where the injection lands and is named in this ticket's file impact. The seam is live today: `:219-222` already injects G5 decomposition context and the no-file-impact declaration. Retrieved candidates are appended there rather than through a new pass, so checkpoint identity, caching and resumption keep working unchanged — a candidate set that changes produces a different `context_digest` and correctly invalidates the checkpoint, which is the behaviour already specified for injected context.

**The budget is a hard cap, not a target.** At most 10 candidates reach the judge and at most 2 LLM calls are spent, per the epic criterion. Retrieval itself is not an LLM call on the lexical tier, so the common case spends its budget entirely on judging. The cap is asserted by a test rather than documented, because an unasserted budget silently grows.

**On demand, not on every review.** Overlap judging is opt-in per run. A plan review that does not ask for it spends 0 additional calls and its checkpoint identity is unchanged, so turning the feature on cannot alter the cost or the cached results of reviews that do not use it.

**Findings are advisory.** An overlap finding reports the candidate ticket and why it overlaps; it does not BLOCK. A ticket that legitimately follows another — a child, a follow-up, a deliberate split — overlaps by construction, so a blocking verdict would stall correct decompositions. The reviewer decides.

**Degradation matches the sibling's.** When the index is absent, catch-up fails, or the configured embedding provider errors, overlap judging is skipped with a diagnostic and the plan review proceeds to its normal verdict. Retrieval cannot change a review's pass or block outcome by failing.

**The injection site has little headroom, so the work is extracted, not appended.** `pass1.py` is 658 lines against the hard cap of 800 in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`, leaving 142 lines. Overlap retrieval and its diagnostic therefore live in a new `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/overlap.py` and `_chunk_extra_context` gains only the call, keeping `pass1.py` under the cap this ticket's own criterion asserts.

Any ratcheted mechanism this adds carries a `# mechanism-ok:` marker at its definition site naming this ticket, since `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` fails on any unadmitted new mechanism.

**Cites re-measured against the merge of Gerrit 3246.** Every line reference in this plan was checked individually rather than sampled: `similar/__init__.py` (91 lines) `:8`, `:46-54`, `:51`, `:52`, `:55`, `:63-64`, `:67-72`, `:73`, `:79-82`, `:83-85`; `pass1.py` (658 lines) `:215`, `:219-222`, `:326`, `:331`, `:339`; `checkpoints.py` (144 lines) `:54`, `:61-63`, `:70`; `passes.py` (510 lines) `:122`; `lexical.py` (120 lines) `:39`. All 21 resolve to the cited construct.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With overlap judging requested, a plan review of a ticket whose plan restates an existing ticket's plan emits an advisory overlap finding naming that ticket. Checked by: a sidecar test over a seeded store asserting the finding is present and names the expected ticket id.
- [ ] Retrieval offers more than 10 candidates on a store seeded with more than 10 matching tickets. This criterion exists because `RESULT_LIMIT` is 5 (`src/rebar/similar/lexical.py:39`), so the retrieval call must raise `limit` above its default or the 10-candidate cap below is vacuously true. Checked by: a sidecar test asserting the retrieval result length exceeds 10.
- [ ] At most 10 candidates are passed to the judge. Checked by: a sidecar test on that same seeded store asserting exactly 10 reached the judge.
- [ ] At most 2 LLM calls are made for overlap judging. Checked by: a sidecar test asserting the call count.
- [ ] With overlap judging not requested, no overlap finding is emitted. Checked by: a test asserting the finding set.
- [ ] With overlap judging not requested, no additional LLM call is made. Checked by: a test asserting the call count is unchanged against the unmodified path.
- [ ] With overlap judging not requested, the run's checkpoint identity is byte-identical to the same review before this change. Checked by: a test comparing the computed checkpoint identity against the unmodified path.
- [ ] An overlap finding never changes a review's verdict from pass to block. Checked by: a test asserting a passing plan's verdict is unchanged when an overlap finding is present.
- [ ] With no model provider configured and no network, overlap retrieval returns candidates from the lexical tier. Checked by: a test clearing provider credentials and asserting a non-empty candidate set reaches the judge boundary.
- [ ] When the index is absent, the plan review completes with its normal verdict. Checked by: a test asserting the verdict equals the verdict of the same review with overlap judging not requested.
- [ ] When the index is absent, a diagnostic naming the absent index is recorded in place of an overlap finding. Checked by: a test asserting the diagnostic is present and the overlap finding set is empty.
- [ ] When catch-up raises, the plan review completes with its normal verdict. Checked by: a test asserting the verdict equals the verdict of the same review with overlap judging not requested.
- [ ] When catch-up raises, a diagnostic naming the catch-up failure is recorded in place of an overlap finding. Checked by: a test asserting the diagnostic is present and the overlap finding set is empty.
- [ ] Every module added or modified under `src/rebar/` is at most 800 lines. Checked by: the CI module-size gate.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0. Checked by: running it.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0. Checked by: running it.
